LinkedIn post angle: A ride-hailing platform sells convenience, but it must manage the risk economics behind every mile.

Company profile: Ford's electric-vehicle division developing and manufacturing EVs alongside its profitable internal-combustion and commercial-vehicle businesses.
Documented business problem: Ford Model e recorded a multi-billion-dollar operating loss amid EV price competition, investment and slower-than-expected adoption.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The challenge is to build EV scale while battery, manufacturing and customer acquisition costs remain high and market pricing is moving quickly.
Business impact / signal: Ford reported Model e losses and adjusted investment and product plans.
Documented company / regulator response: The SEC filing gives the segment result and market context.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Stage EV investment by contribution margin, localise battery sourcing and prioritise platforms with clear customer demand and scale economics.
LinkedIn post angle: A strategic transition can be necessary and still destroy value if the cost curve is not managed.

Company profile: US commission-free brokerage platform whose business and operations are linked to clearinghouse collateral and high-volume retail trading.
Documented business problem: During the January 2021 market volatility, Robinhood restricted certain transactions after increased deposit requirements and liquidity pressures.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): A frictionless customer experience can be interrupted by back-end clearing and collateral obligations if the firm has not built enough capital and liquidity resilience for peak volatility.
Business impact / signal: Robinhood disclosed trading restrictions, customer dissatisfaction and related regulatory and litigation exposure in its IPO filing.
Documented company / regulator response: The SEC S-1 details the restrictions and business risks.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Stress-test intraday collateral needs, maintain liquidity buffers and communicate the reason for restrictions transparently before customer trust is damaged.
LinkedIn post angle: The app can feel instant, but the financial plumbing behind it is not optional.

Company profile: Global short-term rental marketplace connecting hosts and guests across different regulatory environments.
Documented business problem: Airbnb disclosed risks involving unsafe or misrepresented listings, fraud, parties and trust incidents across its marketplace.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The platform does not own most of the inventory, so it must create consistent trust standards across millions of independent hosts and guests.
Business impact / signal: Airbnb expanded identity verification, risk screening, anti-party controls, AirCover and 24/7 support.
Documented company / regulator response: The 10-K describes trust and safety risks and the company's response programmes.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Measure incidents per booking, repeat offenders, response time and resolution quality; make safety outcomes visible to hosts and guests.
LinkedIn post angle: The more asset-light the platform, the more important its trust infrastructure becomes.

Company profile: Indian quick-commerce business operating dark stores and rapid delivery for grocery and everyday essentials.
Documented business problem: Instamart had to improve contribution margin while balancing order growth, average order value, subsidies and store expansion.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): Fast delivery and dense inventory create convenience but also high fulfilment costs. Low-AOV orders can consume capacity without generating enough contribution.
Business impact / signal: Swiggy's shareholder letter described improving contribution margin and reducing unprofitable low-AOV orders while shifting acquisition spend toward more sustainable customers.
Documented company / regulator response: The company shareholder letter gives the disclosed margin trajectory and strategy changes.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Segment customers by order economics, set basket thresholds and measure store-level contribution after picker, rider, shrinkage and discount costs.
LinkedIn post angle: In quick commerce, a 10-minute promise is meaningless if every order loses money.

Company profile: Indian automaker launched the Nano as a low-cost small car intended to expand four-wheeler ownership.
Documented business problem: The Nano attracted attention as the world's cheapest car but demand remained weak; the plant operated well below capacity and production was curtailed.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The 'cheapest car' positioning created status and safety perceptions that may have conflicted with the aspirational purpose of moving two-wheeler households into cars.
Business impact / signal: Tata tried product changes and repositioning but could not create sustained demand; production was later discontinued.
Documented company / regulator response: Ivey and INSEAD case materials document low demand and execution/positioning challenges.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Test the customer's desired identity and use case, not only the price ceiling; build the product promise around dignity, safety and reliability.
LinkedIn post angle: The cheapest product is not always the best value proposition.

Company profile: Global subscription-streaming service with a large catalogue of films, series and games.
Documented business problem: Netflix experienced a difficult growth period and introduced an ad-supported plan and a new approach to account sharing to reaccelerate growth.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The company faced saturation in some markets, price sensitivity and revenue leakage from shared accounts; the fix required adding price points rather than relying only on subscriber additions.
Business impact / signal: Netflix launched a lower-priced ad-supported tier and implemented a more structured account-sharing approach.
Documented company / regulator response: Netflix's 2022 annual review in its proxy statement documents the strategy and member base.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Build tiered monetisation around willingness to pay, improve content discovery and measure retention by household cohort and plan type.
LinkedIn post angle: When subscriber growth slows, the next question is how to earn more value from the audience you already have.

Company profile: Indian telecom operator competing with Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel in a capital-intensive market.
Documented business problem: Vodafone Idea faced a large Adjusted Gross Revenue liability, negative net worth and heavy spectrum-related obligations that constrained investment capacity.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The company must fund network capex and customer experience while servicing long-dated statutory and spectrum obligations; weak network quality can in turn hurt revenue and cash generation.
Business impact / signal: In 2026 the government reassessed AGR dues and set a long repayment schedule; the company continued fundraising and network investment efforts.
Documented company / regulator response: The company's exchange filing and rating report describe the revised dues, payment schedule and liquidity implications.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Prioritise capex by customer density and revenue potential, protect cash runway and publish measurable coverage, churn and ARPU milestones.
LinkedIn post angle: For a telecom operator, debt service and network quality are connected: underinvesting to save cash can worsen the revenue problem.

Company profile: Japanese global automaker with a reputation built around quality and reliability.
Documented business problem: Toyota recalled nearly eight million vehicles in the US for accelerator-pedal and floor-mat entrapment issues and faced criticism over delayed and incomplete disclosure.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The crisis combined mechanical defects with a failure to communicate and escalate safety information transparently to regulators and customers.
Business impact / signal: Toyota recalled affected vehicles, accepted responsibility in a US deferred-prosecution agreement and paid a $1.2bn penalty.
Documented company / regulator response: The US DOJ release documents the company's acknowledged conduct and agreement.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Centralise defect reporting, keep an auditable timeline from first signal to recall and give the safety organisation authority to stop sales.
LinkedIn post angle: Quality reputation is not protection from failure; it raises the expectation for how transparently you respond.

Company profile: Japanese automotive-safety supplier whose airbag inflators were used by multiple global automakers.
Documented business problem: Takata falsified test data relating to airbag inflators and failed to act on internal warnings about data integrity and engineering issues.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): Production deadlines, weak compliance authority and tolerance of falsified test reports undermined the quality system at the supplier level.
Business impact / signal: The company entered bankruptcy proceedings in 2017; the US DOJ brought criminal charges and secured a guilty plea and penalties.
Documented company / regulator response: The DOJ document details internal-control and compliance failures.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Protect quality staff from production pressure, independently validate test data and audit supplier whistleblower and escalation systems.
LinkedIn post angle: A supplier's misconduct becomes an industry-wide safety crisis when the OEM cannot independently verify critical components.

Company profile: Global oil and gas company operating complex offshore drilling projects.
Documented business problem: The Macondo well blowout caused an explosion, loss of life and a major oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The investigation examined risk assessment, change management and the way safety policies were implemented across business units and contractors.
Business impact / signal: BP adopted and expanded its Operating Management System and faced extensive remediation, compensation and regulatory requirements.
Documented company / regulator response: The US Coast Guard / Department of Interior investigation examined BP's policies and operating practices.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Give safety-critical operations independent stop-work authority, verify barrier integrity and audit how written safety systems are actually implemented offshore.
LinkedIn post angle: A safety policy is only real when the frontline can stop the operation without fear.

Company profile: Boeing's 737-9 MAX aircraft experienced a door-plug blowout shortly after take-off in January 2024.
Documented business problem: The incident exposed manufacturing and process-control questions around installation and documentation of the door plug.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The deeper problem is process assurance: if critical installation work is not traceable and independently checked, a completed aircraft can carry unresolved quality risk.
Business impact / signal: The FAA grounded affected aircraft, performed inspections and required a 90-day quality and safety plan.
Documented company / regulator response: The FAA's official update documents the grounding, audit and oversight response.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Require digital work instructions, independent sign-off for safety-critical tasks and serial-number-level traceability from supplier through final assembly.
LinkedIn post angle: A checklist is not a control if nobody can prove it was completed correctly.

Company profile: Global coffee chain with its largest markets in the US and China and annual sales above $36bn in FY2024.
Documented business problem: The company faced repeated quarterly traffic declines and weaker same-store sales in major markets, prompting a leadership change and a new turnaround agenda.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The challenge combined customer wait times, value perception, menu complexity and organisational execution across a large store network.
Business impact / signal: The company introduced a 'Back to Starbucks' direction and operational changes under CEO Brian Niccol; the turnaround remained in progress in the 2026 case study.
Documented company / regulator response: IMD's 2026 case study records the traffic and revenue decline and evaluates the first year of the turnaround.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Simplify the menu and workflow, restore staffing to demand patterns, measure order accuracy and wait time, and test value perception by customer segment.
LinkedIn post angle: When customer traffic falls, do not start with a marketing campaign. Start by asking what the customer experiences in the store.

Company profile: Social networking platform that was once the largest in the world before Facebook overtook it.
Documented business problem: MySpace rapidly lost users after Facebook overtook it, while intrusive advertising and a weaker user experience hurt engagement.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The platform prioritised near-term ad monetisation and a cluttered product experience while a competitor improved usability and social graph utility.
Business impact / signal: News Corp sold MySpace in 2011 for a small fraction of its 2005 purchase price; the business pivoted toward music and entertainment.
Documented company / regulator response: The UK government's digital-platform report documents user decline and cites the role of ad-led short-termism.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Protect core user experience, limit intrusive monetisation and run product experiments based on retention and network health rather than ad inventory alone.
LinkedIn post angle: A network effect can reverse when users begin to leave—and advertising can accelerate the exit.

Company profile: Indian organised-retail group operating Big Bazaar and other formats under the Future Group umbrella.
Documented business problem: Future Retail entered insolvency after failing to repay obligations and was admitted to liquidation in July 2024 after no resolution plan was approved.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The company faced a combination of debt, operating pressure and a failed restructuring path; prolonged uncertainty can damage vendor confidence and asset value.
Business impact / signal: NCLT ordered liquidation and appointed a liquidator in July 2024.
Documented company / regulator response: The company's stock-exchange disclosure confirms the liquidation order and date.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: In a distressed retailer, protect vendor continuity, inventory realisation and store-level cash controls early; do not wait until the resolution window is exhausted.
LinkedIn post angle: A turnaround is not just a plan. It needs a credible buyer, cash runway and stakeholder alignment before time runs out.
Evidence type: Primary – company exchange filing / NCLT order

Company profile: Early social-networking company that grew rapidly before losing users to MySpace and Facebook.
Documented business problem: Friendster's user base declined as users shifted to alternatives with stronger features and better network experience.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): In social networks, value depends on users' connections and activity. When friends move together, network effects can accelerate both growth and decline.
Business impact / signal: Friendster pivoted its business focus and later sold its social-network assets; the user decline became a widely studied network-effects example.
Documented company / regulator response: An ACCC expert report describes how Friendster lost users as alternatives improved.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Track active connections, cohort retention and friend-network migration—not just sign-ups; fix performance and core social actions before adding monetisation.
LinkedIn post angle: For a network business, user churn is contagious because customers do not leave alone.

Company profile: Intel's data-centre and AI accelerator business competing in a market with fast product cycles and strong incumbents.
Documented business problem: Intel recorded a large inventory-related charge associated with Gaudi AI products, signalling a mismatch between inventory commitments and realised demand or product competitiveness.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): In fast-moving hardware markets, production and procurement plans can become obsolete quickly if customer adoption, software ecosystem and performance do not meet expectations.
Business impact / signal: The SEC filing reports the inventory charge and broader manufacturing and competitive pressures.
Documented company / regulator response: The filing provides a direct financial signal; the precise product-specific demand drivers should be described as analysis rather than a quoted management explanation.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Tie AI-chip production to customer qualification and purchase commitments, stage inventory buys and measure software ecosystem adoption alongside silicon performance.
LinkedIn post angle: In AI hardware, demand forecasts can expire faster than the inventory sitting in the warehouse.

Company profile: Jet Airways acquired Air Sahara in 2007 and later operated the low-cost JetLite brand.
Documented business problem: The Air Sahara acquisition increased financial and integration complexity while Jet faced a rapidly changing low-cost airline market.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The acquisition added scale but did not automatically create a coherent fleet, brand, cost and network strategy; integration costs compounded the pressure from low-cost competition.
Business impact / signal: Jet's operating model struggled to recover profitability and the airline eventually suspended operations in 2019.
Documented company / regulator response: Academic case analysis describes the acquisition burden, competition and strategic mismatch.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Before acquiring scale, test integration synergies, fleet compatibility and the post-deal cost curve; establish a 100-day integration scorecard with stop/go gates.
LinkedIn post angle: An acquisition should make the operating model simpler or stronger—not just make the company bigger.

Company profile: Kingfisher acquired low-cost airline Air Deccan and later tried to manage premium and low-cost positioning under one group.
Documented business problem: The acquisition brought a low-cost carrier into a premium airline group, creating integration and positioning challenges.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The two businesses had different customer promises, fleet economics and operating disciplines. Combining them without a clear architecture made the cost base and brand story harder to manage.
Business impact / signal: Kingfisher later grounded operations amid debt, unpaid dues and ongoing operating issues.
Documented company / regulator response: Academic case material describes the Air Deccan acquisition, business-model transition and resulting strain.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Keep separate brands only when economics and customer propositions truly differ; otherwise design a clear operating model before integrating networks and fleets.
LinkedIn post angle: Buying a different business model is not the same as knowing how to operate it.
Evidence type: Academic case study / credible business-school source

Company profile: Netflix's subscription business had substantial viewing by people outside the paying household.
Documented business problem: Netflix identified widespread account sharing as a monetisation problem and introduced paid-sharing measures alongside plan changes.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The challenge was balancing revenue leakage with customer backlash: monetising shared usage can increase paid accounts but also increase cancellations if execution is too aggressive.
Business impact / signal: Netflix implemented paid-sharing rules and introduced a lower-priced ad-supported plan.
Documented company / regulator response: The company describes the strategy in its 2022 year-in-review filing.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Roll out account changes by market with clear communication, household verification grace periods and churn monitoring by cohort.
LinkedIn post angle: Turning free usage into paid usage only works when the user still feels the value is fair.

Company profile: Vodafone Idea is a nationwide telecom operator with substantial statutory and spectrum-related payment obligations.
Documented business problem: The reassessment of AGR dues improved visibility but left a long repayment schedule and a need for continued capex and funding.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): Debt rescheduling can create time, but not operating competitiveness. The company still needs enough network investment to retain customers and generate cash.
Business impact / signal: The Department of Telecommunications finalised a revised AGR amount and staggered repayments over multiple years; the company disclosed the schedule.
Documented company / regulator response: The May 2026 exchange filing describes the finalised dues and payment schedule.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Treat debt relief as runway, not the turnaround; publish quarterly milestones for 5G coverage, churn, ARPU, capex productivity and free cash flow.
LinkedIn post angle: A liability extension buys time. Only a better operating business creates a sustainable turnaround.

Company profile: MySpace was a major social platform before Facebook overtook it in global users.
Documented business problem: MySpace's user decline coincided with an increasingly cluttered ad experience and a strategy that placed short-term revenue ahead of user experience.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): Network businesses rely on interaction quality and habit. Monetisation that degrades the core experience can create a feedback loop of user loss and reduced advertiser value.
Business impact / signal: News Corp sold MySpace in 2011; the platform was repositioned toward entertainment and music.
Documented company / regulator response: The UK government digital markets report summarises the user decline and the short-term advertising critique.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Set monetisation guardrails around page performance, user retention and ad frequency; protect the core user experience before maximising ad load.
LinkedIn post angle: In a network business, the user experience is the asset. Advertising is only how you monetise it.

Company profile: Japanese diversified electronics and infrastructure group with businesses spanning energy, devices, semiconductors and infrastructure.
Documented business problem: An independent investigation found inappropriate accounting across several business areas, including project accounting, expenses, inventory valuation and parts transactions.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The investigation identified strong pressure to meet profit targets, top-management involvement and failures in board, audit and internal-control checks.
Business impact / signal: Senior executives resigned; Toshiba created governance and management-revitalisation structures and published recurrence-prevention measures.
Documented company / regulator response: Toshiba's independent investigation report and company improvement plan describe the causes and corrective actions.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Remove unrealistic profit targets, strengthen independent audit authority, test percentage-of-completion assumptions and protect escalation channels from executive pressure.
LinkedIn post angle: A target that cannot be achieved operationally can turn into a control failure when leadership refuses to reset it.
Evidence type: Primary – company investigation / official remediation plan

Company profile: Google's wearable-computing project introduced a head-mounted display for consumers and later pivoted toward enterprise and specialist applications.
Documented business problem: Google Glass failed to gain broad consumer adoption; the product offered limited everyday utility while raising privacy, social-acceptance and price concerns.
Root-cause analysis (interpretation): The development process underweighted real-world customer context. A technically novel interface did not solve a frequent enough problem to justify wearing it in public.
Business impact / signal: The consumer Explorer programme ended; Google later focused Glass on enterprise and industrial use cases.
Documented company / regulator response: US National Science Foundation research summarises the innovation failure, root causes and pivot.
Recommended management fix (not necessar: Prototype in the real environment, validate a high-frequency job-to-be-done and test social acceptance and privacy before scaling a hardware launch.
LinkedIn post angle: The market does not reward novelty by itself. It rewards usefulness people are comfortable adopting.
